To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure-property relationships of bicarbazoles were studied by extensive experimental and theoretical methods.
the structure-property relationships of a series of bicarbazoles, namely 1-12 were investigated.
the connection of two carbazole units at the 3-positions via an acetylene linker leads to a highly fluorescent compound, which has a very low oxidation potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the systematic investigations of the structure-property relationships of a series of carbazole dimers (bicarbazoles) and provides valuable information for the development of carbazole-containing materials.
the synthesis of a series of conjugate carbazole dimers and their structural and electronic properties.
the design, synthesis, structure-property investigations, and applications of a large series of novel conjugated carbazole derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electronic properties of 1–12 can be systematically tuned by the structural modifications.

the electronic and photophysical properties of the carbazole dimers can be tuned in a broad range by varying the conjugation connectivity, the length and the nature of the spacer, and the substitution pattern of the two carbazole units.
the electronic and photophysical properties of the bicarbazoles can be tuned by the conjugation connectivities, π-conjugated spacer length, and donor strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure-property relationship of bicarbazoles is mainly determined by the connection position of the two carbazole units, the π-conjugation extent of the whole system, and the electron-donatibility of the system.
the structure-property relationships for the carbazole dimers are highly complicated.

a systematic investigation of the structure-property relationships on a series of bicarbazoles has been carried out, and that the electronic and photophysical properties of the bicarbazoles can be tuned by the conjugation connectivity, the spacer length, and the spacer structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure-property relationship of the bicarbazoles is highly tunable, thus allowing the design and synthesis of bicarbazoles with desirable electronic properties.
the electronic and photophysical properties of the carbazole dimers can be finely controlled by the conjugation connectivity, spacer, and substituents.
the structure-property relationship of carbazoles can be tuned in a wide range by varying their conjugation patterns and spacers.
